⚠️ Part of Android itself, not an ordinary app. Shizuku cannot block it — Android refuses firewall rules for its own components. Root can, but where the user ID is shared with a protected app, such as Settings, it also needs \'Allow Firewall Critical Packages\' enabled in Settings and will affect those apps too.
⚠️ Background Check could not determine this app\'s user ID in its profile, so no firewall rule can be applied to it.

⚠️ This app is in another profile. The current firewall mode works with app names inside the profile Background Check runs in, so it cannot reach this one. Use ConnectivityManager with Shizuku or root for independent profiles, or run Background Check inside this profile to use its VPN.

⚠️ This app is in another profile. The current firewall mode blocks an app in every profile at once, so this copy follows the switches of the same app in the profile Background Check runs in. Root access blocks each profile on its own.

⚠️ This app shares a user ID with a protected app, and the current firewall mode blocks by user ID, not by app. Blocking it would cut off the protected app too, so Background Check leaves the whole user ID alone. To block it anyway, enable \'Allow Firewall Critical Packages\' in Settings and then turn on the switch for this app.

⚠️ Background Check protects this app\'s user ID, so the Block All default is not applied to it — doing so could cut off a protected system app. With \'Allow Firewall Critical Packages\' enabled you can still block it: turn on the switch for this app.

⚠️ Another app shares this app\'s user ID and has a firewall rule of its own. The current firewall mode blocks by user ID, so that rule applies to this app too, including any block while the screen is off. The switches in this sheet are this app\'s own settings.
